23|SOC without abiraterone, the addition of abiraterone

33|groups, compared with 104 (74%) of 141 and 65 (46%)

35|(appendix p 14). Prostate-cancer-specific survival was
36|also improved by the addition of abiraterone in the ADT
37|with docetaxel population (median 4·72 years vs not
38|reached; HR 0·69, 95% CI 0·53-0·90; p=0·0062;

40|Adding abiraterone to ADT with docetaxel (with or
41|without radiotherapy) had no effect on the number of
42|docetaxel cycles administered (median 6 [IQR 6-6] in
43|both groups). 138 (61%) of 226 patients in the ADT with
44|docetaxel population and 183 (53%) of 347 in the ADT
45|without docetaxel population had abiraterone treatment
46|discontinued, including 29 (21%) of 138 and 32 (17%) of
47|183 due to toxicity, respectively (appendix p 14). Overall,
48|the median abiraterone treatment duration before
49|discontinuation was 33·2 months (95% CI 25·5-43·2) in
50|the ADT without docetaxel population and 34·1 months
51|(30·0-43·5) in the ADT with docetaxel population.
52|In the ADT with docetaxel safety population, 217 (63%)
53|of 347 patients who received abiraterone versus 181 (52%)

55|one severe adverse event (grade 3 or worse) and
56|seven (2%) versus three (1%) had a fatal adverse event
57|(table 3, appendix p 14). In the ADT without docetaxel
58|population, 149 (66%) of 226 patients who received
59|abiraterone had at least one severe adverse event and
60|eight (4%) had a fatal adverse event (table 2). Therefore,
61|the addition of docetaxel to abiraterone did not increase
62|the incidence of severe or fatal adverse events. In the
63|ADT with docetaxel population, 49 severe adverse events
64|occurred per 100 person-years in patients who received
65|abiraterone compared with 55 per 100 person-years in
66|patients who did not receive abiraterone (appendix p 14).

68|or worse adverse events that were reported in ≥5% of

70|abiraterone and patients who did not in the ADT with
71|docetaxel population, except for hypertension (76 [22%]
72|of 347 patients vs 45 [13%] of 350) and hepatotoxicity with
73|increased aminotransferases (20 [6%] of 347 vs two [1%]
74|of 350), which were more frequent among those who
75|received abiraterone (table 3). Although the incidence of
76|severe hypertension and hepatotoxicity were similar in
77|patients who received abiraterone in the ADT with
78|docetaxel and ADT without docetaxel populations, there
79|was a difference, as expected, in the incidence of severe
80|neutropenia, which occurred in 34 (10%) of 347 patients
81|versus none of 226, respectively (appendix p 15).
82|Although severe fatigue and peripheral neuropathy
83|events did not reach the frequency cutoff of 5% in the
84|ADT with docetaxel population, ten (3%) of 347 patients
85|who received abiraterone and 15 (4%) of 350 who did
86|not receive abiraterone had at least one event of severe
87|fatigue, and four (1%) and six (2%) had at least one
88|severe peripheral neuropathy event (table 3).

4|Discussion
5|To our knowledge, this is the first trial to show that a
6|triple systemic therapy, consisting of ADT, docetaxel,
7|and a second-generation androgen signalling inhibitor
8|(abiraterone), extends radiographic progression-free survival
9|and overall survival in patients with de novo mCSPC.
10|Whether the systemic treatment of high-volume disease
11|(ie, extended metastatic spread) should differ from that of
12|low-volume disease has been extensively debated. The
13|benefit of ADT with docetaxel has been clearly shown for
14|patients with mCSPC with high-volume disease,4,22 but
15|data collected from larger populations support a similar
16|benefit across high-volume and low-volume disease.3 This
17|discrepancy might result from different ratios of patients
18|with de novo versus relapsing low-volume disease being
19|included in these trials, because recurrences favour better
20|prognoses.23 Second-generation androgen receptor axis
21|inhibitors have shown overall survival benefits in patients
22|with mCSPC regardless of the disease volume
23|considered.5,9,10 In this trial, the mature data for men with
24|high-volume disease indicate a clear improvement in
25|both radiographic progression-free survival and overall
26|survival when abiraterone is added to ADT with docetaxel.
27|Even though the data on overall survival were immature
28|for patients with low-volume disease, an abiraterone-
29|mediated benefit in radiographic progression-free
30|survival was already apparent. Thus, ADT with docetaxel
31|plus abiraterone should be proposed as a new SOC for
32|patients presenting with high-volume disease who are fit
33|for docetaxel prescription. However, for patients with low-
34|volume disease, the decision of whether to use two or
35|three agents should be carefully considered by both the
36|patients and their oncologists, to determine whether a
37|major benefit in radiographic progression-free survival
38|(HR 0·58) is sufficient to justify a treatment inten
39|sification in a context of immature overall survival data. It
40|would also depend on whether an overall survival benefit
41|is required. Long-term data and consensus conferences
42|will allow for clinical practice guidance refinement.
43|As abiraterone can inhibit CYP3A4 in vitro,24 and as
44|CYP3A4 is involved in docetaxel elimination,25 the
45|concomitant administration of these two drugs could
46|potentially increase docetaxel exposure and thereby its
47|toxicity. However, no increase in chemotherapy-related
48|side-effects occurred in reaction to this concomitance,
49|which might suggest an absence of substantial drug-
50|drug interactions between abiraterone and docetaxel.
51|This finding is consistent with the observation that
52|abiraterone and docetaxel have similar pharmacokinetic
53|behaviour when administered alone or in combination.26
54|Similarly, abiraterone did not affect the clearance of
55|another taxane, cabazitaxel, by CYP3A.27 We also did not
56|observe an increase in haematological toxicity when
57|abiraterone was added to ADT with docetaxel, contrary to
58|a phase 2 trial in patients with mCRPC.28 The most
59|frequent high-grade adverse event reported among
60|patients who received abiraterone in this trial was
61|hypertension (22% of patients who received abiraterone
62|vs 13% of those who did not). This expected adverse event
63|was carefully monitored and managed to prevent the
64|onset of cardiovascular events, which were not seen in
65|excess in this trial. In the ENZAMET trial,10 hypertension

26|open-label trials, the rapid clinical practice evolution
27|for mCSPC that took place during the conduct of
28|this trial prompted the sequential amendment of the

30|those changes, answer meaningful questions, and
31|implement the best treatment options to all participants

33|benefit for patients with mCSPC treated with abiraterone

40|allocating men to ADT only would have been unethical,

In addition, they do not display absolute cross- 7|resistance, as abiraterone improves overall survival 8|after docetaxel treatment and docetaxel retains some 9|activity after abiraterone failure.30,31 Collectively, these 10|observations provide a rationale for the survival benefits 11|resulting from their combination in this trial. However, 12|this study did not answer whether this triple 13|combination yields clinical advantages over ADT plus a 14|second-generation androgen receptor axis inhibitor. 15|Indeed, at the time when this trial was conducted 16|(2013-18), combining ADT with such an inhibitor had 17|not been approved for mCSPC, thereby precluding 18|such a comparison within the trial. Incidentally, the 19|ongoing phase 3 ARASENS (NCT02799602) and 20|ENZAMET (NCT02446405) trials are also testing the 21|combined efficacy of second-generation androgen 22|receptor axis inhibitors (darolutamide and enzalutamide, 23|respectively) with ADT and docetaxel, and their 24|upcoming overall survival results will put the benefits 25|of abiraterone in perspective. 26|Reaching treatment synergy and preventing acquired 27|resistance despite tumour clonal heterogeneity are 28|cardinal aspects of mCSPC management that require 29|an optimisation of the treatment framework.
